title: Are you unhappy at work?
reason: 从昨日的消费与数字生活轮换到工作生活平衡和团队管理。节目用英国职场与建筑行业试验讨论工作强度、管理方式和任务制工作，贴合工程管理、项目交付和团队协作场景。练习围绕六个高频表达反复调用，从原文支撑的回忆逐步过渡到改写、受限项目场景应用和有限自由表达。

targetExpressions.meaning: lose energy or enthusiasm because of working too hard
targetExpressions.usage: Engineers can get burned out if urgent work continues for too long.

targetExpressions.meaning: finish required work by the agreed time or date
targetExpressions.usage: The team simplified the release scope to meet the deadline.

targetExpressions.meaning: watch someone very closely and repeatedly check what they are doing
targetExpressions.usage: People may work less confidently when a manager is breathing down their neck.

targetExpressions.meaning: move from one approach or habit towards a different one
targetExpressions.usage: The project shifted away from measuring hours and focused on completed tasks.

targetExpressions.meaning: by the planned date and without spending more than planned
targetExpressions.usage: Clear priorities helped us deliver the migration on time and on budget.

targetExpressions.meaning: a situation or result that benefits everyone involved
targetExpressions.usage: Flexible on-call scheduling can be a win-win for staff and the service.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does it mean when someone gets burned out at work?

options.text: They lose energy or enthusiasm after working too hard.
They finish every task earlier than planned.
They change to a better-paid department.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript defines burnout as lacking energy or enthusiasm because of working too hard.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the reusable project expression: We reduced the scope so that we could ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme discusses pressure to meet deadlines; 'meet a deadline' means finish the required work by the agreed time.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: If a supervisor is 'breathing down your neck', what are they doing?

options.text: Watching and checking your work very closely.
Giving you complete control over your schedule.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil explains that the idiom means someone is watching you very closely and checking everything you do.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Emma Stewart's change in approach: The trial tried to ______ presenteeism and towards task-based work.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Emma says the construction trial shifted away from presenteeism to an output-based, task-based way of working.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What happened to the construction projects under the task-based trial?

options.text: They were delivered on time and on budget.
They were stopped because workers went home earlier.
They required more overtime and more money.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Emma reports that the projects were delivered on time and on budget while workers also reduced overtime.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the conclusion: Better delivery and improved work-life balance made the trial ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme calls flexible, task-based working a win-win because it helps both project delivery and workers.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why does the programme criticise presenteeism?

options.text: Long hours used to show commitment are not necessarily an effective way to work.
Workers are never allowed to finish tasks at home.
Every task-based project goes over budget.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Beth says staying longer merely to show that you work hard is not effective, while the task-based approach achieved strong results.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the workplace warning: Constant pressure and overtime can cause experienced staff to ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: This is a natural transfer of the transcript's explanation that working too hard can leave people without energy or enthusiasm.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Retell the episode in 80-120 words without looking at the full transcript. Use this structure: (1) topic - why some jobs make people unhappy; (2) two key ideas - pressure and close supervision, then the construction industry's task-based trial; (3) conclusion or example - how flexible working affected delivery and workers. Phrase bank: 'get burned out', 'shift away from something', 'a win-win'. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, clear English is enough; advanced vocabulary and complex sentences are not required.
referencePoints: People can be unhappy in jobs that are boring, badly paid or so demanding that they become burned out.
British work culture can emphasise fast pace, targets and deadlines, with supervisors closely checking workers.
A good job uses people's talents and gives them some choice over how and when they work.
The construction trial shifted away from presenteeism and used a task-based approach instead of measuring long hours.
Workers could go home after completing their agreed tasks well while still receiving the same daily pay.
The projects were delivered on time and on budget, overtime fell and work-life balance scores doubled.
